react_result.final_narrative_text: Four complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00052 / SMPDB:SMP00043 / KEGG:map00052 / MUMM:galactose_metabolism) as the dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned Galactose Metabolism as rank 1 (SMPDB namespace) and rank 2 (KEGG namespace) with FDR 1.72e-12, fold-enrichment 1,089×, driven by five input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00052 as its top hit with unadjusted p-value 5.16e-08, overlapping the same five compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis placed 'galactose_metabolism' at rank 5 (p=0.018) with 12 overlapping metabolites, achieving 92% pathway coverage. The five driver metabolites are galactitol (KEGG:C01697), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116); InChIKey reconciliation across all five confirmed zero structural conflicts, ruling out namespace artefacts. Glycerophospholipid metabolism emerged as a secondary consensus: mummichog ranked it rank 4 (p=0.011) and RaMP ranked it rank 5 (FDR 2.6e-05), with three shared driver metabolites (myo-inositol, ethanolamine, glycerol). Glycerol bridges both the galactose and glycerophospholipid pathways, acting as a substrate in Leloir pathway flux and as a backbone precursor for phospholipid biosynthesis. MetaboAnalystR also flagged Ascorbate and aldarate metabolism (p=0.044) with myo-inositol as the sole overlapping metabolite, reflecting myo-inositol's dual membership in both pathways. Dopamine, 2-methoxyestradiol, squalene, and inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate did not reach significance in any single paradigm, indicating they are not primary drivers of the treatment effect.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Four complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00052 / SMPDB:SMP00043 / KEGG:map00052 / MUMM:galactose_metabolism) as the dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned Galactose Metabolism as rank 1 (SMPDB namespace) and rank 2 (KEGG namespace) with FDR 1.72e-12, fold-enrichment 1,089×, driven by five input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00052 as its top hit with unadjusted p-value 5.16e-08, overlapping the same five compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis placed 'galactose_metabolism' at rank 5 (p=0.018) with 12 overlapping metabolites, achieving 92% pathway coverage. The five driver metabolites are galactitol (KEGG:C01697), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116); InChIKey reconciliation across all five confirmed zero structural conflicts, ruling out namespace artefacts. Glycerophospholipid metabolism emerged as a secondary consensus: mummichog ranked it rank 4 (p=0.011) and RaMP ranked it rank 5 (FDR 2.6e-05), with three shared driver metabolites (myo-inositol, ethanolamine, glycerol). Glycerol bridges both the galactose and glycerophospholipid pathways, acting as a substrate in Leloir pathway flux and as a backbone precursor for phospholipid biosynthesis. MetaboAnalystR also flagged Ascorbate and aldarate metabolism (p=0.044) with myo-inositol as the sole overlapping metabolite, reflecting myo-inositol's dual membership in both pathways. Dopamine, 2-methoxyestradiol, squalene, and inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate did not reach significance in any single paradigm, indicating they are not primary drivers of the treatment effect.
